text:
Samuel Girard's week was defined by one play. His cross-check on Boston's James Hagens on Nov. 5 sent the rookie out of the game; the Bruins have since put Hagens on injured reserve for "a few weeks," according to NHL.com. We won't guess at intent. It's the context anyone watching Girard right now will carry.

On the ice, he's been better than his raw line. He has 7 points in 14 games for Pittsburgh, a points rate of 1.57 per 60 minutes that's above our range for him, but the Penguins have scored 7.4 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. That should come back.

Evolving-Hockey had him 34th among 215 defensemen last season with a strong offensive contribution, though it came with very strong teammates in Colorado (95th percentile). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking puts him in the 86th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists. He won a Cup with the Avalanche in 2022. We project about 31 points. His minutes, just under 20 a night, are holding steady.
headline: Girard and the Hagens hit
